producer_report.summary: I added an `audience` role and an `athena audience [--target <url>] [--json]` command. It reads a published page as a newcomer would and commits an `athena.audience-rating/1` record: target, audience, a rating from 1 to 5, and findings that each cite a source. A rating of 2 or below also queues a proposal work item, which `athena status` lists and the owner can approve or reject. `athena status` and the steward's brief show the latest rating per target with its findings. The role reads and records only. The default target is a new `[audience] target` in `athena.toml`, set to the doodla/athena Pages address taken from Cargo.toml's `repository`, so the owner name is in config, not code. I did not run the real agent or fetch a real page: tests use the fake agent and a stubbed page, with no network. fmt, clippy and the full test run all pass.

checks_run.note: Run as `cargo test --locked --quiet --no-fail-fast`: every test binary passed, including crates/athena-cli/tests/audience.rs (7 tests) and the xtask policy and boundary tests. An earlier run failed on a key-order assertion in my new schema test; I fixed that test and reran the whole suite.

open_issues: Nothing starts the role by its cadence. The definition records `cadence_tasks = 20`, but the role runs only on `athena audience`. The brief let me choose a CLI command or cadence, and I chose the command to keep the change small. The design page says so.
The role is not live-tested. Whether `claude -p` honors WebFetch with this policy and allow rule, and what rating the real model gives, is unverified.
The default target's owner name comes from Cargo.toml's `repository` field, not from a live Pages check. If the real Pages URL differs, change `[audience] target` in `athena.toml`.

I edited files outside the listed deliverables: `config.rs`, `outputs.rs`, `store.rs`, `display.rs`, `policy.rs`, `fake.rs`, and the match arms in `run_pin_tests.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` and `tests/retry.rs`. Each was needed for the role to compile, parse, be recorded or be shown. `wiring.rs` needed no change.
`athena audience` exits 2 for a rating of 2 or below. The header comment in `main.rs` does not list this exit code.
The audience always runs as `newcomer`. The record has an `audience` field, but the command cannot name another audience yet.
`docs/architecture.md` still says 'twelve record types' and 'three roles' in its crate table; I did not change those lines.
I did not touch `docs/design/requirements-map.md` and marked no row.
mistakes: My first version of the schema test asserted the order of `required`; it failed on the first full run and I fixed it.
I mistyped a path in one Read call; the policy hook denied it and nothing was affected.
learnings: The tool policy denies WebFetch to every role. The brief assumed the agent could fetch through its allowed read tools, so I added a narrow allowance in `policy.rs` for the audience only, for plain https addresses. The driver builds `--allowedTools` only from Bash commands, so `audience::run` adds a `WebFetch` permission rule to the invocation spec itself.
Adding a `Role` variant breaks exhaustive matches in `fake.rs`, `run_pin_tests.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` and `tests/retry.rs`. None of those are in the deliverable list.

The steward's invocation records live under a job-shaped directory, but the store files steward runs apart from jobs. I did the same for the audience with new `audience_runs` and `audience_ratings` fields.
The `Config` parser denies unknown fields, so a new `[audience]` table needed a config.rs change. I put it after `[landing]` so the existing landing test that splits on `[landing]` is unaffected.
Schema `required` lists come out in alphabetical order, so tests must not assert their order.
The Bash tool here refuses sed, tail and pipes; only the listed cargo, git and file commands run.
desires: A way to try the real `claude -p` WebFetch once, to confirm the page is fetched and the allow rule is honored.
Permission to use sed and tail, to read long cargo output without rerunning it.
